finding.claim: DELETE /files/<fid> performs no effective authorization check: is_allowed returns a bool that is discarded, so any caller can delete any stored file.
finding.source: Any request to DELETE /files/<fid>, with any value (or no value) in X-Session-User-Verified.
finding.sink: del STORE[fid] (views.py:19), a protected destructive operation.

trace.note: load_user copies the request header into g.user without verification
require_allowed (alias of is_allowed) called; return value ignored
is_allowed returns a boolean and never raises

finding.guards_checked: before_request load_user (views.py:10-12) only copies the header. is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) returns a bool with no abort. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10), which does abort(403), is not used on this route. No other decorator or middleware is present. Rename route (views.py:26) does enforce the check, so the two routes are inconsistent.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. views.py:10-12 (load_user) only copies the X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user with no verification. acl.py:4-5 (is_allowed) returns a bool and never aborts. views.py:18 calls require_allowed (alias of is_allowed) as a bare statement, so the result is discarded. acl.py:8-10 (ensure_allowed, which aborts with 403) is imported but not used on the DELETE route. No other decorator or middleware exists in the two files.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at views.py:18 discards the bool from is_allowed (acl.py:4-5), so line 19 `del STORE[fid]` runs for any caller, including anonymous ones, while the rename route at views.py:26 correctly uses ensure_allowed, which aborts with 403.

finding.claim: The caller's identity is taken from an unverified client header, so any client can impersonate any user holding grants.
finding.sink: g.user used as the principal for authorization decisions at views.py:18 and views.py:26 via acl.py:5 (grants.get(user)).

trace.note: ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'write') on the rename route
grants.get(user, []) keyed by the attacker-supplied identity

finding.guards_checked: No verification of the header exists in this code. The header name suggests an upstream gateway verifies it, but no such gateway is visible in the repo. Impact depends on whether a trusted proxy strips and overwrites this header. This is an authentication weakness and is flagged explicitly per org policy.

verdict.guard_found: None verify the header. views.py:12 copies X-Session-User-Verified straight into g.user with no check. The only authorization check is acl.py:8-10 ensure_allowed, which aborts with 403 at views.py:26, but it trusts whatever identity it receives. Also, views.py:18 calls is_allowed (acl.py:4 import alias require_allowed), which returns a bool that is discarded, so the delete route has no effective check at all. That is a separate bug the candidate's sink description overstates.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 takes the caller identity directly from a request header with no verification, and views.py:26 with acl.py:5 then authorizes on that value, so any client that sets the header to a granted user can pass the rename check. Reachability is anonymous, but only if no upstream gateway strips and overwrites the header, which the repo does not show; the candidate's trace lines are accurate, and the cited line 18 is a discarded boolean rather than an effective check.
